text:
Mira: quick heads-up — nightly perf shows a regression in the concatenated attention kernel after the post-attention writeback change. P50 ~+4%, P99 ~+12% for long sequences (seq=1024+).
Sam: repro command?
Mira: run this on a single GPU: 
```
./bench_attn --model=gpt-small --seq=2048 --batch=4 --kernels=concat_v2,scalar_base --iters=200 --profile=nvprof
```
Mira: concat_v2 is the new kernel with writeback fusion (bias+rotary applied into pack store). scalar_base is the previous path.
Arian: saw logs. nvprof shows L2 read/write spike when concat_v2 runs. can you paste the counts?
Mira: pasted sample profiler extract below (trimmed):
```
KERNEL: concat_v2  GPU time 1.98ms  SM eff 0.86  L2 reads 42MB  L2 writes 6.1MB  DRAM reads 120MB
KERNEL: scalar_base GPU time 1.74ms  SM eff 0.91  L2 reads 18MB  L2 writes 2.2MB  DRAM reads 88MB
```
Mira: so concat_v2 increases L2 traffic ~2x which aligns with the P99 regress.
Noah: hypothesis: the fused store layout is misaligned with the pack buffer stride so stores are causing write-amplification and extra cacheline churn. also batching heuristics produce mixed-length coalescing that hurts the writeback path.
Sam: interesting — did you try aligning the pack base to 128 bytes as a quick check?
Mira: yes — aligning pack base improves L2 writes ~30% and cuts P99 to +6%, but still worse than scalar_base. full numbers:
```
concat_v2 aligned: GPU time 1.82ms  L2 reads 30MB  L2 writes 4.3MB
scalar_base:        GPU time 1.74ms  L2 reads 18MB  L2 writes 2.2MB
```
Arian: what about small sequence case? does concat_v2 still regress for seq<=256?
Mira: for short sequences concat_v2 is slightly faster (P50 -6%) — regression only appears for sequences >512 and batch mix with many short+long in same batcher window.
Noah: sounds like a KV cache interaction — paged-KV allocator evicts lines when convo lengths vary, then the fused writeback path thrashes L2. we should check paged-kv hit/miss ratio during the run.
Mira: added paged-kv counters — hit_ratio drops from 0.88 -> 0.62 under concat_v2 for mixed batches.
Sam: actionable next steps: 1) add simple guard to disable writeback fusion when seq>512 or batch contains mixed lengths; 2) experiment with 128B alignment by default; 3) run a microbench where the batcher groups same-length only.
Arian: I can add a config flag: runtime.fuse.post_writeback = auto|on|off (default auto). For auto, early bail when mixed-length detected. I'll make a small patch.
Mira: thanks. patch + perf harness results would be great. If guard fixes P99, we can keep fusion for short workloads and iterate on packing layout.
Noah: long-term idea: change packing layout to be row-major contiguous for stores and keep the bias/rope apply in-register until after coalesced store. Might add a small register op cost but reduce L2 churn.
Sam: also tune batcher: group requests by seq length bucket for fused kernel path. We already have len_buckets but the heuristic threshold might be too permissive. Try len_bucket_max_gap=64 for fused path.
Mira: running two experiments now: (A) runtime guard disabling fusion for mixed batches, (B) 128B alignment + stricter buckets. will post numbers in ~20m.
deploy-bot: nightly-build 2750001200 completed — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/attn-bench/2750001200/
Mira: linking artifacts: https://s3.redwood/attn-bench/2750001200/concat_v2_profile.txt
Sam: thanks — if (A) fixes it we should ship guard quickly and mark the packing layout work as follow-up.
Arian: agreed. also add a regression test that runs mixed-length workload in CI with concat_v2 enabled (low iter but enough to catch L2 blowup).
Noah: I can prototype the row-major store patch; might take a day.
Mira: quick note: this failure mode explains a few customer reports about tail latency spikes on multi-turn conversations. good catch.
Sam: ok keep updates short here. major ask: paste final numbers for P50/P95/P99 for both experiments when done. :thumbsup:
Mira: will do — starting runs now.
